one_liner: Jira Cloud has a broad REST v3 API with self-serve OAuth 2.0 (3LO) via the developer console plus basic-auth API tokens, and Atlassian lists a vendor-run Atlassian MCP server.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 (3LO) authorization code grants are for non-Forge/Connect integrations. Basic auth is for personal scripts and ad-hoc calls (API tokens). Connect apps use JWT built into the Connect libraries. Atlassian says apps that collect API tokens or have customers create individual 3LO apps violate its policies, so multi-user toolkits should ship a single distributable 3LO app.
access_notes: OAuth 2.0 (3LO) apps are created in the developer console. The pages do not state pricing explicitly. All apps start in Tier 1 rate limits by default; Tier 2 per-tenant quota requires review. Free-on-all-plans claim is not confirmed by the supplied pages.
blocker_notes: Minor friction: points-based rate limits with Tier 1 default; Tier 2 needs review. Distributable 3LO app needed for multi-user use.
